labels.label: rem:connected

hypotheses.paper: Sigma = Sigma_1 disjoint union Sigma_2, so v = 1_{Sigma_1} in W^{1,2} with grad v = 0 (l.411-412)
hypotheses.note: the model has no topology: carried as some v with energy v = 0; the disconnected witness is discModel (Sigma = {0,1} u {2})
hypothesis ell v != 0; balModel shows the qualifier is load-bearing
MeanPoincare is refuted under TraceBound, finite measures, V != 0 and some |B_j| > 0 (the standing hypotheses of lem:capstar)

findings: Title imprecision, not an error (AUDIT-1 minor): the remark's body is proved and its « ℓ(v) ≠ 0 in general » (l.412) already concedes the balanced case; only the title « Connectedness is necessary » is literally false — rem:connected (l.409-415), the title 'Connectedness is necessary' overstates and 'in general' (l.412) carries the remark: on balModel, two components {0,1} and {2,3}, each an edge with one boundary point of equal area, v = 1_{{2,3}} has zero energy and the Poincare inequality fails, yet ell(v) = 0, cap* = 32 > 0 and eq:capineq holds for every u (Yamabe.CapRemarks.bal_witness). The condition eq:capineq needs is that no union of components Sigma_1 is balanced, |Sigma_1|/|Sigma| = sum over B_j in the boundary of Sigma_1 of w_j. That criterion is argued, not formalized.
questions: What 'Sigma = Sigma_1 disjoint union Sigma_2' means on the measured model (l.411). Reading taken: there is v in D with energy v = 0 and ell(v) != 0. The remark itself derives exactly this from disconnectedness, and it is the only consequence the remark uses.

labels.label: rem:tight

hypotheses.paper: u constant on the boundary (l.566), u >= 0 (standing, l.460)
hypotheses.note: tr u = c a.e. on every B_j, c >= 0; S != 0
ell v = 1, energy v = cap*, 0 < cap* < infinity; also every a v with a >= 0; existence under lem:capstar's hypotheses with DirectMethod (exists_capacitary_eq)
(C1 X + C2 Y)^2 <= (C1^2/a_N + C2^2/c_N)(a_N X^2 + c_N Y^2), the A~ = 0 skeleton of the proof of thm:main (l.519-550)

hypotheses.paper: psi and theta in u = 1 - s psi at s = 1/(1+theta) (l.569-570)
hypotheses.note: psi a competitor of cap_D (the thm:upper psi, l.862); both theta (printed) and theta_D tested

findings: rem:tight, third clause (l.569-570), false as printed. With psi the classical equilibrium potential of l.862, u_s = 1 - s psi realises X/Y = sqrt(cap_D)/(t sqrt S) at s = 1/(1+t). At s = 1/(1+theta), as printed, this equals c_N sqrt(S)/(a_N sqrt(cap*)) iff cap_D = cap* (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.ratio_upperTest_theta_iff). At s = 1/(1+theta_D) it equals c_N sqrt(S)/(a_N sqrt(cap_D)) (ratio_upperTest_thetaD), the printed ratio with cap_D in place of cap*. Counterexample: pathModel, a connected path 0 - 1 - 2 with boundary areas 1 and 4 on which MeanPoincare and TraceBound hold, has cap* = 27 < 54 = cap_D. Neither choice of s realises the printed ratio there, so the Cauchy-Schwarz step is strict at both (Yamabe.CapRemarks.path_rem_tight_counterexample).

rem:tight, first sentence (l.565): 'each of the three inequalities used is an equality for the capacitary profile'. On pathModel the equalities in lem:holder, lem:capacitary and the Cauchy-Schwarz step hold together only at u = 0 (Yamabe.CapRemarks.path_no_tight_profile), so no single tight profile exists. The three clauses do hold one at a time (proved). All three hold together exactly when the eq:capstar minimiser is constant on the boundary, i.e. when cap* = cap_D (e.g. the two-point toy model, cap* = cap_D = 8).
questions: psi at l.570 appears before it is defined (l.862, section 'Optimality'). Reading taken: the classical equilibrium potential of thm:upper (psi = 1 on the boundary, integral of psi = 0). Under the other possible reading (psi a normalised eq:capstar minimiser), u_s is not constant on the boundary, so lem:holder's equality condition, clause (1), fails in general.

Which Cauchy-Schwarz step is meant (l.567). Reading taken: (C1 X + C2 Y)^2 <= (C1^2/a_N + C2^2/c_N)(a_N X^2 + c_N Y^2), whose equality ratio is exactly the printed X/Y. This is the A~ = 0 case of the 2x2 eigenvalue bound. For A~ > 0 the extremal direction of the full quadratic form differs.

labels.label: rem:dichotomy

hypotheses.paper: Sigma compact connected with non-empty boundary, the trace theorem (via thm:main)
hypotheses.note: MeanPoincare, TraceBound, InteriorBump (theta > 0), as in Main.thm_main
SobolevIneq, giving C_SP < infinity through exists_isSobolevPoincareConst
C_SP > 0 for the strict domination; theta > 0 and F_g(1) > 0 are derived
not printed: only its resulting bound A/(1+sqrt(A/B))^2 is stated, and it is proved here from the rank-one bound by the comparison

findings: Model-side hypothesis, not a finding for the author (AUDIT-1 minor): lem:csp-lower gives C_SP > 0 in the paper's setting — rem:dichotomy (l.1030), minor: 'strictly dominates it for every geometry' needs C_SP > 0 (and theta > 0). At C_SP = 0, tau = 0 and the two bounds coincide (Yamabe.dichotomy_lt_rankOne: strict iff theta, F, C > 0). On a manifold with non-empty boundary C_SP >= 2^{1/N} K_sob > 0 by lem:csp-lower (l.333), so the sentence holds in the paper's setting. The planner's [r] identity is verified: the denominators differ by 2 tau (sqrt(1+theta) - 1), with tau^2 = A(1+theta)/B.

kb_proposals: pattern: cheap graph models for the measured model live in Yamabe.CapRemarks (scaffold CapacityRemarks). finModel k n mub e (Fin k, counting measure, flat frame finMetric, val = tr = id, constant differential e) comes with vol, bvol, gradSq, energy, dirichlet and volMean lemmas. edgeMap i j i' j' gives two edges. normSq_count_two and normSq_smul_dirac compute the norms. Disconnected, balanced and asymmetric-boundary examples cost about 30 lines each.

pitfall: norm_num [Matrix.cons_val] does not evaluate ![a,b,c,d] 3 at this pin. simp only [Matrix.cons_val_three, Matrix.cons_val_two, Matrix.cons_val_one, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.tail_cons, Matrix.head_cons] does, and is packaged as CapRemarks.vecLit / vecLit3.
pitfall: IsFiniteMeasure (c • mu) for c : ENNReal has no instance; give it as by exact <by simp>.

pattern: on the measured model cap* < cap_D as soon as the boundary areas are unequal (pathModel: 27 < 54). Statements of the paper that silently identify the eq:capstar minimiser with the classical equilibrium potential psi should be tested there.
notes: One new file, no sorry, no strict edit. The import line was appended to scaffold/YamabeScaffold.lean. lake build YamabeScaffold.CapacityRemarks built only this module. The file imports the strict Yamabe.Perforated.Poincare (for exists_isSobolevPoincareConst) and Yamabe.Perforated.Upper. The finite models are namespaced Yamabe.CapRemarks to avoid generic-name clashes on graduation. No label is marked: rem:connected rests on a reading, rem:tight's third clause and first sentence are refuted on pathModel, and rem:dichotomy carries thm:main's model facts and leaves two asymptotic sentences unformalized.
audit: AUDIT-1 minor: rem:connected recorded as a title imprecision; rem:dichotomy's C_SP > 0 as a model-side hypothesis; rem:tight's refutation confirmed under both readings of ψ (master, at integration).
